claim_rule: Only baseline issue metrics may appear in claims. Topic rollups, monthly trend shares, coverage counts and corrected sensitivity values must be described separately and never exported as claims.
dataset_limits: Historical self-selected app reviews are not the complete customer population.
No revenue, plan tier, confirmed cancellation, or causal retention data is available.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn.
Issue-level sensitivity correction cannot allocate predicted non-complaints into a latent issue.
The adopted grouping retains low_coherence issues even after one bounded split.

evidence_selection_rule: Per issue: the most common severity among member rows (ties -> higher severity); among distinct member texts with that severity, the three closest to the issue centroid by cosine similarity of the saved grouping embeddings.

grouping_comparison.scope: One grouping method is run here. The method was chosen earlier on the full corpus by comparing TF-IDF clustering (v1) with embedding clustering (v2/v3); that comparison is archived in artifacts/full_run_v2/grouping_comparison.json.

I_ACCESS_01.description: Users say the app does not allow them to log in or access their account, with little detail about the cause.

I_ACCESS_02.description: Examples describe trouble accessing the app, music, or playlists, alongside vague reports that something is not working and a device-specific notification issue.

I_ACCESS_03.description: Users specifically report that phone-number login does not work.

I_ACCESS_04.description: Most examples report being unable to install the app, while a few object to installing it or say it should be deleted.

I_ACCESS_05.description: Users report being unable to log in, including failures with phone-number login and repeated errors.

I_ACCESS_06.description: Users report being unable to log in to an existing account, often encountering repeated errors.

I_ACCESS_07.description: Users are signed out, locked out, or rejected when trying to return to an existing account.

I_ACCESS_08.description: Users report being unable to log in, sometimes citing a generic error message or repeated unsuccessful attempts.

I_BILLING_01.description: Reviews broadly object to basic features being moved behind Premium without identifying one specific feature problem.

I_BILLING_02.description: Reviews express dissatisfaction with payment requirements, subscription cost, or inability to afford Premium.

I_BILLING_03.description: Reviews broadly object that many features or functions require Premium, without identifying a specific restricted feature.

I_BILLING_04.description: Users report that core listening controls, including song choice, skipping, or seeking, require Premium.

I_CATALOG_01.description: Most examples report missing songs, while others describe difficulty choosing among many tracks, uninteresting selection, or alleged stream filtering.

I_CATALOG_02.description: Reports include difficulty finding songs, language-specific search or lyrics issues, podcast language mismatch, and missing local files.

I_CATALOG_03.description: Examples mix unwanted or repetitive playback and recommendations with missing songs, playlist behavior, and general catalog praise.

I_CATALOG_04.description: Lyrics are missing, unavailable, or fail to load for songs.

I_CATALOG_05.description: Examples combine unwanted recommendations with ad burden, interface and audio quality complaints, and general praise for the catalog.

I_CATALOG_06.description: Most examples report unavailable or missing songs, while others describe playback restrictions, missing lyrics, or liked songs disappearing.

I_CATALOG_07.description: Most examples say songs are unavailable or absent, with additional reports of search connectivity failure and a specific catalog omission.

I_DOWNLOADS_01.description: Downloaded music is unavailable or cannot be played when the device is offline, despite being saved for offline listening.

I_DOWNLOADS_02.description: Most examples express general dislike without a specific download problem; one reports the app appearing offline while the user is connected.
I_DOWNLOADS_02.issue_name: Vague negative reactions to the app

I_DOWNLOADS_03.description: Reports describe downloads that fail, take too long, or disappear or save to the wrong storage location.

I_DOWNLOADS_04.description: Most examples report downloaded songs disappearing, alongside reports of offline playback failing or downloads moving to internal storage.

I_DOWNLOADS_05.description: Reports cover missing or difficult downloads, download restrictions and limits, repeated downloads, offline access, and finding downloaded tracks.

I_OTHER_01.description: Reviews give brief, nonspecific negative assessments without describing a product problem.

I_OTHER_02.description: These reviews broadly dislike the app without describing a specific product problem.

I_OTHER_03.description: These reviews express general dissatisfaction with a recent update but do not identify a specific change or problem.

I_PLAYBACK_01.description: Music playback stops, pauses, or fails to start, sometimes requiring users to restart the app, switch tracks, or reinstall it.

I_PLAYBACK_02.description: The app intermittently freezes, crashes, stops responding, or stops working during playback across devices.
I_PLAYBACK_02.issue_name: App freezes, crashes, or stops responding

I_PLAYBACK_03.description: Reports describe songs failing to play as selected, unexpected track choices or repetition, and playback advancing or becoming silent.

I_SUPPORT_01.description: Users describe customer service as very poor, with one report that chat takes too long to connect.

I_SUPPORT_02.description: Users report support failing to address account access concerns, including unhelpful automated interactions.

I_SUPPORT_03.description: Users report difficulty reaching support or getting useful help and resolution.

I_SUPPORT_04.description: Users describe support as unresponsive, ineffective, or unable to resolve problems.

I_SUPPORT_05.description: Users report support responses that are poor, dismissive, ineffective, or absent.

I_SUPPORT_06.description: Examples mix difficulty canceling or disconnecting subscriptions with completed cancellations and general intent to cancel.

I_SUPPORT_07.description: The example is an abusive expression of dissatisfaction without a specific support problem.

I_SUPPORT_08.description: Reviewers report difficulty reaching Spotify support, receiving responses, or getting their issues resolved.

I_SUPPORT_09.description: Users report poor support that is difficult to reach and unhelpful when contacted.

I_USABILITY_01.description: Users report ads appearing too frequently during music or podcast listening.

I_USABILITY_02.description: Reviews mention shuffle behavior and limits on choosing or playing songs, but also mix in playlist changes and song selection issues that are not specific to shuffle.

I_USABILITY_03.description: Examples consistently say that ads are too frequent or excessive.

I_USABILITY_04.description: Most examples complain that Spotify adds recommended or unwanted songs to playlists, while others describe song selection limits or missing library content.

I_USABILITY_05.description: Reports describe removed or changed features and a degraded interface after updates, with one separate Android Auto voice command issue.

monthly_trend.context_only: Trend figures may qualify the recommendation but are never claims.
monthly_trend.rule: share = complaint_or_cancellation_rows / classified_rows per calendar month; the first and last months of the input are treated as partial

limitations: The verifier is an independent model pass, not human ground truth.
The local stratum has 290 verified texts; sparse cells depend on smoothing.
Bootstrap intervals represent verifier-sample uncertainty under this correction model, not total model uncertainty.
Issue corrections cannot recover false-negative complaints into a specific issue because they were never grouped.
These corrected estimates are sensitivity outputs and are not claims.csv evidence.
